headline: Impairment charge drives net loss; FFO guidance holds

drivers.explanation: Same-property NOI fell 10.6% as average occupancy declined from 92.6% to 87.1%, driven by previously disclosed key lease expirations with downtime aggregating over 900,000 RSF.

Swing to a loss driven by $222.5M of impairment charges on real estate reclassified as held for sale, including a Sorrento Mesa land parcel, a Canadian operating property, and a vacant Cambridge office building.
Mirrors the net-income swing; driven by the same $222.5M impairment charge on assets reclassified as held for sale.

Reflects temporary borrowings under the commercial paper program used to fund the April repayment of $350M of maturing unsecured senior notes, to be repaid via planned dispositions and other capital sources.
Quarter shaped by held-for-sale impairments and continued occupancy softness from prior lease expirations, while leasing volume rose 60% q/q and full-year FFO guidance held its midpoint.

summary_short: Alexandria's Q2 2026 revenue fell 13% y/y to $662.8M and the company swung to a $72.8M net loss (diluted EPS -$0.43) from a $361.7M Q1 profit, mainly on $222.5M of impairment charges tied to properties reclassified as held for sale.
summary_long: Revenue fell 13% y/y and 1% q/q to $662.8M as same-property NOI dropped 10.6% on average occupancy sliding from 92.6% to 87.1%; period-end occupancy was 86.9%. Net loss of $72.8M reflects $222.5M of impairment charges on properties moved to held-for-sale, including assets in Sorrento Mesa, Cambridge, and Canada. FFO per share, as adjusted, was $1.73. Alexandria narrowed full-year 2026 FFO-per-share guidance to $6.35-$6.45, holding the $6.40 midpoint; occupancy and same-property NOI guidance were unchanged. Total cash rose q/q to $470.4M and long-term debt rose to $12.81B on temporary commercial-paper borrowings; shareholders' equity slipped to $15.55B. The dividend held at $0.72/share; the $500M buyback authorization remains unused.
